fix: Every input event is cloned into the recursion-diagnostics state, and only Text(String) and Ime carry heap data, so each keystroke or IME event allocates. Avoid the clone on the input path: have handle_input take the event by value and store a Copy-able trigger summary (pointer phase/position, key data, or a char count for Text/Ime) in recursion.rs instead of InputEvent. Alternatively store the event only while diagnostics are enabled. Keep diagnostic_input_trigger formatting lazy at report time.

The nested match repeats the Pointer* variants as unreachable!() arms and ends in an early return. Move the non-pointer handling into a helper, e.g. fn handle_non_pointer_input(&mut self, event: InputEvent) -> Option<EventTarget> containing the Scroll/Key/Text/Ime/TrackpadGesture/WindowResized arms, and in the destructuring match write `other => return self.handle_non_pointer_input(other),`. This removes the three unreachable!() arms and one nesting level. No behavior change.
